# TexPrep RE

> Free Texas real estate exam prep — study guides, a free practice quiz, and the TexPrep RE iOS app with 1,900+ TREC-specific practice questions.

Facts on these pages are verified against primary sources (DRE / TREC / DBPR / Pearson VUE) and dated. Fee and format figures reflect the current schedules as of the date shown on each page.

## Study guides & exam facts

- [Hardest Texas Real Estate Exam Topics (TREC Data)](https://texprepre.com/hardest-topics.html): Over half of first-time test takers fail the Texas real estate exam. We break down the hardest TX TREC exam topics by official pass rate data — so you know exactly where to focus.
- [How Long Does It Take to Get a Texas Real Estate License?](https://texprepre.com/how-long.html): Most people: 3–6 months, dominated by the 180-hour education requirement (six 30-hour courses; TREC caps coursework at 12 hours/day — a 15-day legal floor). TREC application ($206) and IDEMIA fingerprints ($37) can overlap the courses; TREC posts live processing dates and an application status tracker; exam results are same-day. As of July 2026 a DPS fingerprint-processing delay makes early fingerprinting the key move.
- [Texas Real Estate License Reciprocity: There Isn't Any — But There's a Shortcut](https://texprepre.com/reciprocity.html): Texas has no real estate reciprocity with any state (TREC's official answer). But agents actively licensed in an ARELLO-accredited state can waive the national exam portion by submitting a license history with their TREC application — leaving only the 40-question Texas portion (28 to pass). No "license transfer" exists; education, fingerprints, exam, and broker sponsorship still required.
- [Texas Real Estate Exam Math: Formulas & What's Actually on the Test](https://texprepre.com/math.html): Only 7–9 math questions on the Texas real estate exam — all on the national portion, none on state. Key formulas, worked examples, and what you can safely skip — so you walk in confident.
- [I Failed the Texas Real Estate Exam](https://texprepre.com/fail.html): Failed the Texas real estate exam? Here's exactly how the retake works — the $43 fee, the one-year/three-attempt window, why you only retake the portion you failed, and how to pass next time.
- [Texas Real Estate Exam Vocabulary: 50 Terms You Need to Know](https://texprepre.com/vocab.html): The 50 most-tested Texas real estate exam terms — from IABS and intermediary representation to the rule of capture — with plain-English, exam-focused definitions organized by topic.
- [Free Texas Real Estate Practice Questions](https://texprepre.com/practice-questions.html): 20 free Texas real estate exam practice questions with answers and explanations — covering license law, agency, contracts, finance, appraisal, and more. National + state portions, no email required.
- [How Many Questions Is the Texas Real Estate Exam? Format, Time Limit & Passing Score](https://texprepre.com/exam-facts.html): The Texas real estate sales agent exam is 125 questions (85 national + 40 state, plus unscored pretest items) with a 4-hour total time limit — you need 70% on each portion. Full format, fees, and retake rules.
- [How Much Does It Cost to Get a Texas Real Estate License? (2026 Fee Breakdown)](https://texprepre.com/cost.html): Expect $590–$1,290 all-in: $300–$1,000 for the required 180-hour courses, $206 TREC application, $43 exam fee, and $37 fingerprinting. Full itemized fee table inside.

- [Free Texas Real Estate Practice Exam](https://texprepre.com/quiz.html): Take our free 16-question Texas real estate practice exam. Find your weak spots across key TREC exam topics and see exactly where to focus your studying. No email required.
